title: Give it a rest: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis on the effect of inter-set rest interval duration on muscle hypertrophy
publication: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
population: 9 randomized studies in healthy adults (19 measurements: 10 thigh, 6 arm, 3 whole body).
key_findings: Growth overlapped substantially across short, intermediate, long and very long rest periods, with considerable heterogeneity.
Direct comparisons tended to favour rests longer than 60 seconds for the arm and thigh, while whole-body estimates were near zero and marginally favoured shorter rests.

No appreciable further difference appeared beyond about 90 seconds; whether sets went to failure did not change the picture. The authors suggest any small benefit of longer rest may work through preserved volume load.
methods: Systematic review with Bayesian hierarchical meta-analyses of randomized studies that changed only the rest interval, registered on OSF.
limitations: Nine studies with wide credible intervals and heterogeneous results; the suggested mechanism is the authors' interpretation.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
